title: Ang 1168–1171: Basant begins
hookLine: Guru Nanak opens the spring raga
tomorrow: spring comes for everyone. why does a Guru say only for some?
last: RAVIDAS: WHAT IS SEEN WILL PASS.

cards: The first warm afternoon after a long gray stretch: windows open, somebody's mowing, a bird you forgot existed starts up again. Nobody decides to feel lighter. It just happens.
Turn the page from Ravidas, to ang 1168, and the Granth does the same thing. A new raga starts, Basant, the spring raga, and Guru Nanak opens it.

teach.h: BLESSED IS THE MONTH SPRING COMES.
teach.b: In paraphrase, Guru Nanak's first Basant hymn begins: of all the months, blessed is the one when spring comes, and stays.
Blossom, my mind, remembering the Lord, always. Listen to the twist. Real spring leaves.

teach.h: FOREVER SPRING: NOT IN THE CALENDAR.
teach.b: This one is called forever spring, sadaa basant, because it isn't in the calendar. It's in the mind that remembers.
Something to tell a friend tonight: in the Granth, the spring raga comes straight after the serious morning one, with no gap at all: Ravidas's last line on one page, and spring on the next.

teach.h: A WEEK OF BHAIRAO, LOOKING BACK.
teach.b: And that's a good way to look back on the week, because every hymn we read in Bhairao was about where to put the mind. Nothing outside the One. One clay, many pots.
I serve the One. A wealth not knotted, not sold. A cup of milk, meant.
Six lines from one morning raga, and now the spring raga picks up the same thread: blossom, remembering.

how: Ragis sing Basant hymns in kirtan, especially around the coming of spring; readers find Guru Nanak's opening Basant hymns at ang 1168 under the heading Mahala 1.

s: in Guru Nanak's Basant hymn, spring is only about the weather
his spring is a mind that blossoms, remembering the Lord: forever spring.
Basant begins right after Bhairao in the Granth
Ravidas closes Bhairao on ang 1167; Basant begins on ang 1168.
Guru Arjan's 'not Hindu, nor Muslim' line has only one accepted reading
some Sikh readers hear a distinct path; others hear the One past every label.

games.q: a friend is in a long, gray season of life: nothing's growing. she reads Guru Nanak's line about forever spring. what's it offering her?
o: a spring the mind can carry, remembering, whatever the month.
a promise that the hard season will be over by spring.
a reminder to celebrate the spring festival this year.
games.why: Guru Nanak's 'forever spring' isn't in the calendar. it's the mind that blossoms, remembering the Lord.

practice: Find one living thing you can see from where you are: a plant on a shelf, a tree through the window, a weed in a crack. Look at it for this sit, and look for one thing about it that's growing.
If you'd like, read ang 1168 before you begin.

carryVoice: Spring, the Basant kind: a season the mind can carry into any month. Week done. Next week, more spring.
